edges.note: The selected direction is a new verification-audit line from verified G7. It is not the frozen G8 candidate 001 and does not reuse its blocked status-only strict-verdict provenance interface. No formal run has occurred.

nodes.statement: Across the frozen G0-G7 series, strict passes range from 30 to 37 and known strict fails from 13 to 21 over the fixed 56, with 2-3 completed strict-verdict unknowns per generation. G3-G7 improve structural provenance and timeout localization but do not establish answer-verification effects or causal gain. The bounded problem is whether a task-agnostic pre-terminal evidence-answer audit can reduce the known strict-fail queue without increasing timeout or other terminal failures under exact 56-task, base-description, no-hint, 1200-second, strict/56 scoring.

nodes.falsification_condition: Mechanism is contradicted if any non-timeout cohort has a negative audit task, if prohibited content is persisted, if behavior changes outside the intended return_answer path, or if a first return_answer is dispatched or evaluated before audit. With mechanism support, the directional outcome is contradicted if strict pass is at most 31 or timeout plus other terminal failure is at least 5. A strict pass of 32 with an unchanged queue is inconclusive, not confirmed. No strict-verdict unknown is converted into a failure or a pass.
nodes.prediction: In one formal 56-task no-hint run with the fixed 1200 s limit and strict all-56 scoring with timeouts and other terminal failures counted as failures: (1) non-timeout cohorts each reach at least 0.8 audit-positive coverage; (2) strict pass is at least 33; (3) timeout plus other terminal failure is at most 4; (4) no prohibited content is persisted and no behavior changes outside the return_answer audit path; (5) completed strict-verdict unknowns remain unknown and are not reclassified.
nodes.statement: In a new child of the verified G7 code parent, intercepting the first return_answer proposal with one generic evidence-answer audit instruction and allowing a later return_answer to terminate will produce a strict-pass count above the G7 reference of 32 over the fixed 56, with the timeout plus other terminal failure queue not above 4, no protocol violation, and at least 0.8 audit-exposure coverage in each non-timeout cohort. The mechanism claim is exposure only; the score association is descriptive and not causal because the run is unpaired.

nodes.frozen_evaluation: Exactly one formal candidate evaluation over the same frozen 56 no-hint tasks, the same single 1200 s per-task wall limit, the same harness and evidence-integrity binding, and strict pass over all 56 tasks with timeouts and other terminal failures counted as failures. No task is added, removed, re-scored, or reinterpreted; completed strict-verdict unknowns remain unknown; no answer, hint, validator, held-out data, or prior graph is read; no second arm, sham run, or probe run is added. The child partition and audit-exposure counts are compared descriptively with the G7 reference of 32 strict pass, 17 known strict fail, 3 completed strict-verdict unknown, and 4 timeout plus other terminal failure. The run is unpaired, so no causal claim is made.
nodes.interface_status: unverified: the G7 parent and DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call observation hook are verified, and return_answer is an existing tool, but one-time interception and generic message injection at that hook are not verified. This design does not use the blocked status-only strict-verdict provenance enum and does not read feedback.answer_quality, validators, answers, hints, or task content. If the hook cannot inject the generic audit instruction without reading answer arguments or changing other dispatch behavior, do not launch.
nodes.intervention: Add one runner hook at the existing DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call pre-exec boundary in a new child of verified G7. On the first return_answer proposal for a task, do not dispatch it; inject one generic, task-agnostic audit instruction that asks the agent to re-check the proposed answer against tool observations already in its context and repair or return it; set audit_requested=true. Dispatch a later return_answer normally so it can terminate the task. Read only tool_name and the hook-local step ordinal for this decision. Do not read or persist return_answer arguments, messages, results, task IDs, answers, hints, validators, raw traces, credentials, or task content. Do not change the task set, 1200 s limit, tool set, tool dispatch outside the first return_answer, result storage, error handling, or scoring. If the first return_answer cannot be intercepted and the audit instruction cannot be injected without reading answer content or changing other behavior, do not launch.

measurement_plan.aggregation: Report task counts and rates separately for strict pass, known strict fail, completed strict-verdict unknown, and timeout or other terminal failure, always with the fixed 56 as the outcome denominator. Report audit-positive, audit-negative, and audit-unknown counts separately for each observed cohort, with numerator, denominator, and rate. Never pool cohorts to hide missing coverage. Compare descriptively with the G7 reference and the G0-G6 table; do not infer causality, correctness, or priority.
measurement_plan.contradicted_conditions: Mechanism is contradicted if any audit-negative task exists, prohibited content is persisted, behavior changes outside the intended return_answer path, or a first return_answer is dispatched or evaluated before audit. With mechanism support, the directional outcome is contradicted if strict pass is at most 31 or timeout plus other terminal failure is at least 5.

coverage.rule: For each observed non-timeout cohort, coverage is audit-positive tasks divided by that cohort's observed denominator. Coverage below 0.8 withholds mechanism support for that cohort and is inconclusive, not a launch veto. Timeout and other terminal failure tasks are not forced into a non-timeout coverage rate.
coverage.timeout_or_other_terminal_failure: reported separately; no rate threshold; no terminal return_answer is audit-unknown

denominators.cohort_denominators: observed task counts in strict pass, known strict fail, completed strict-verdict unknown, and timeout or other terminal failure after the frozen evaluator join

hooks: DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call pre-exec: intercept the first return_answer, inject one generic audit instruction, set audit_requested, and allow a later return_answer to terminate
measurement_plan.inconclusive_conditions: The result is inconclusive if any non-timeout cohort has coverage below 0.8, no audit request is observed, the injection interface is unavailable, strict pass is exactly 32 with an unchanged queue, or too many timeout or unknown tasks prevent cohort assessment. Completed strict-verdict unknown tasks are reported separately and are not reclassified; timeouts and other terminal failures remain failures.
limitations: The audit instruction is generic; the packet cannot verify that the agent actually performs a meaningful audit without reading answer or message content.
The design measures audit exposure, not audit quality, correctness, or causal benefit.
The run is unpaired and compares only descriptively with the G7 reference.
The return_answer interception and message-injection interface is unverified.
Only one formal run is allowed; no run-to-run variance estimate is available.
Completed strict-verdict unknowns remain unknown and timeouts remain failures.
No answer, hint, validator, raw trace, task content, credentials, or network access is used.
measurement_plan.per_task_negative_rule: A task is audit-negative if a terminal return_answer is observed without audit_requested, the first return_answer is dispatched or evaluated before audit, the audit request occurs after terminal, the later terminal return_answer is not permitted, prohibited content is persisted, or agent-visible behavior changes outside the return_answer audit path.
measurement_plan.per_task_positive_rule: A task is audit-positive when a pre-exec return_answer is observed, audit_requested is set for the first such proposal, a later terminal return_answer is observed at a greater hook ordinal, no prohibited content is persisted, and no behavior outside the return_answer audit path changes. Audit-positive is mechanism exposure, not correctness; a task may be audit-positive and still be a known strict fail.
measurement_plan.per_task_unknown_rule: A task is audit-unknown if no terminal return_answer is observed, including timeout or other terminal failure before a terminal answer; the sidecar record is missing; the hook injection failed; hook ordinals are ambiguous; or trace completeness is insufficient. Unknown is never imputed as audit-positive, audit-negative, strict pass, or strict fail.
measurement_plan.run_before: All rules, cohort labels, denominators, the 0.8 coverage threshold, the G7 reference counts, supported and contradicted conditions, and unknown fallbacks are fixed before child implementation or formal execution; no post-run strict verdict, task ID, answer, hint, or validator defines a rule. This selection step performs no formal evaluation.
measurement_plan.supported_conditions: Mechanism is supported if each non-timeout cohort has audit-positive coverage at least 0.8 and no audit-negative task. The descriptive outcome association is supported if mechanism is supported, strict pass is at least 33, timeout plus other terminal failure is at most 4, and no protocol violation occurs. This is not a causal claim.

nodes.negative_control: A scope guard, not a second arm. Prelaunch enabled-versus-disabled hook tests must show that the only behavioral difference is the intended first-return_answer interception and generic audit injection, with identical tool dispatch elsewhere, identical results, identical timing limit, and identical scoring. In the formal run, audit-positive tasks require audit_requested and a later terminal return_answer; if the audit binds on zero tasks, the mechanism is untested. Any agent-visible read, prohibited content persistence, or behavior change outside the return_answer path invalidates the experiment.
nodes.no_answer_no_hint_boundary: The hook may read only tool_name and hook-local step ordinal at execution and may write only anonymous_task_index, hook_local_step_ordinal, return_answer_ordinal, audit_requested, later_terminal_return_answer_seen, coverage_status, and sidecar_terminal_status. It must not persist, log, expose, or otherwise use benchmark answers, hints, validators, expected outputs, task IDs, raw traces, messages, tool results, raw argument payloads, raw tool names, credentials, network content, digest strings, or task content. The injected instruction is generic and task-agnostic and contains no answer or task hint. Cohort labels and strict verdicts are joined only after the run from the frozen evaluator and are never read by the agent or hook during execution.

limits: Audit exposure is structural; semantic verification quality is not observed.
A later return_answer in the same model response can precede model-visible audit feedback.
Timeouts are failures in fixed 56; unavailable records remain unknown.
Three completed strict verdicts remain unknown and are not reclassified.
This is one unpaired run; score differences from earlier generations are descriptive only.
nodes.statement: G8 generic pre-terminal return_answer verification audit on the frozen no-hint 56.
